sections.title: Manage the boxes of a hive

items.back:
Definition: A hive is a stack of boxes: the brood box at the bottom where the queen lays, and honey boxes above it.
Category: 7.1 Hive boxes
Key Points: Brood below, honey above; parts between the boxes control who moves where

Definition: A flat grid with gaps wide enough for worker bees but too narrow for the larger queen, fitted between the brood box and the honey boxes above it.
Example: A beekeeper fits one above the brood box in spring so the honey boxes hold only honey and no brood.
Category: 7.1 Hive boxes > Between the boxes
Key Points: Workers pass, the queen cannot; it keeps eggs and brood out of the honey boxes; it stays on all season, unlike a bee escape board

Definition: A board with a one-way exit, placed under the honey boxes a day or two before harvest, so bees can leave those boxes but cannot find their way back in.
Example: The evening before harvest, a beekeeper slides one under the full honey boxes, and the next morning they are almost empty of bees.
Category: 7.1 Hive boxes > Between the boxes
Key Points: One way, so it clears bees out; used only for a day or two before harvest; it does not sort bees by size like a queen excluder
